content.comment_body: I have a reliable 24VDC power supply ([company_name]) that powers our input devices like switches and sensors to activate inputs. The problem is, many controls are positioned far from the controller, and we occasionally get random reports of stray voltages triggering the digital inputs. These incidents are unpredictable and very difficult to diagnose. We don’t install or control the type of cabling used between the control devices and the controller. I’ve managed to lessen the effect by adding pull-down resistors from each input to 0V, but I’m really searching for a plug-in device that could streamline this process—something that avoids the extra soldering or assembly work. Does [company_name] or anyone else offer a plug-in input filtering module for the [product_name]?

Hello [user_name], As mentioned, using pull-down resistors after shielded wires is one of the best options. When all inputs are in a high state, how do you reset them? It might be a hardware issue. If possible, can you try replacing the [product_name] controller with a new unit? Good luck.

When I build a panel that includes a [product_name] or other controllers, and I’m not doing the rest of the installation (like cabling), I prefer to invest a little in auxiliary relays, which serve to transfer the input signals. It costs about 6-8 euros per input. These relays are compact (about 6mm wide) and available at many retailers. They act as loads and help filter out false signals in similar situations. [url]

Install power supply units close to the sensors and other devices. Ensure you have a reliable, dedicated wire between every 0V terminal of the distant PSU and the [product_name]. Use screened cables for transmitting data from sensors to the [product_name], and ground the cable screen only at the [product_name] PSU side. Don’t use the screen for signal transmission—instead, use two wires for the signals. Continue using the pull-down resistors as well. Good luck!

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter sporadic false digital input activations on [product_name] modules due to stray voltages, especially over long cable runs. Methods like pull-down resistors provide some relief, but there’s a clear need for a modular, plug-and-play filtering solution. Currently, there is no dedicated hardware filter module available for these inputs, so users rely on workarounds rather than a purpose-made [company_name] accessory.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] or a third-party manufacturer to offer a simple, modular, or plug-in digital input filter compatible with [product_name] modules, making it easy to prevent false signals without extra assembly or complex modifications.
